`dsFlowerClient` submits declarative model specifications to data nodes running
`dsFlower`. The analyst chooses the valid computation; each node independently
owns its per-training epsilon, delta, clipping and executable policy.

## Connect to DataSHIELD

```r
library(dsFlowerClient)
library(DSI)
library(DSOpal)

builder <- DSI::newDSLoginBuilder()
builder$append(
  server = "site1",
  url = "https://opal1.example.org",
  user = "researcher",
  password = "...",
  table = "PROJECT.training_data",
  driver = "OpalDriver"
)

conns <- DSI::datashield.login(
  logins = builder$build(),
  assign = TRUE,
  symbol = "D"
)
```

## Fit a declarative model

```r
fit <- ds.flower.fit(
  conns,
  symbol = "D",
  target = "outcome",
  features = c("age", "cholesterol", "heart_rate"),
  model = "pytorch_logreg",
  rounds = 5L,
  feature_bounds = list(
    lower = c(18, 50, 30),
    upper = c(100, 400, 220)
  )
)
```

`feature_bounds` are optional data-independent constants from public domain
knowledge or the study protocol. They must follow feature order. The node never
returns exact counts, sums, variances or quantiles for preprocessing. Training
and prediction use the same clipped affine transform.

Before submission, the client verifies that all nodes expose runner ABI 3 and
the exact recursive SHA-256 of its bundled canonical runner. The client does not
send privacy parameters.

## Direct submission API

Use `ds.flower.submit()` when the explicit submission arguments are useful:

```r
fit <- ds.flower.submit(
  conns,
  model = ds.flower.model("pytorch_mlp", hidden_layers = c(64, 32)),
  symbol = "D",
  target = "outcome",
  features = c("age", "cholesterol", "heart_rate"),
  num_rounds = 10L,
  strategy = "fedadam",
  feature_bounds = list(
    lower = c(18, 50, 30),
    upper = c(100, 400, 220)
  )
)
```

Aggregation strategy is post-processing of already-private node updates and is
not an analyst privacy knob.

## Right-censored survival

The custodian must configure patient privacy with a stable subject identifier.
Use baseline covariates and two ordered outcome columns: time in days from
baseline, then event (1 = event, 0 = right-censored). Public time bounds and
fixed dispersion are chosen before inspecting private outcomes.

```r
survival_model <- ds.flower.model.pytorch_aft(
  horizon = 3650, time_scale = 365,
  distribution = "weibull", dispersion = 1
)
# Alternatively, ten public intervals and one K-output head per subject:
# survival_model <- ds.flower.model.pytorch_discrete_hazard(
#   edges = seq(0, 3650, by = 365))

survival_fit <- ds.flower.fit(
  conns, symbol = "D", model = survival_model,
  target = c("followup_days", "event"),
  features = c("age", "cholesterol", "heart_rate"),
  feature_bounds = list(lower = c(18, 50, 30), upper = c(100, 400, 220)),
  rounds = 5L
)
# public_test contains only public or independently authorized local data.
risk <- ds.flower.predict(survival_fit, public_test, type = "risk")
curves <- ds.flower.predict(
  survival_fit, public_test, type = "survival", times = c(365, 730, 1825))
```

Private validation, holdout, CV and survival training inside HPO fail before
node contact. Evaluate the released model on a disjoint public or authorized
local test set. The [survival article](survival-segmentation.html) defines
interval endpoints, invalid-record totalization and local prediction semantics.

## Outputs and diagnostics

The intended output is the DP global-model artifact returned by the Flower run.
Nodes expose neither losses, counts, failures, timing nor raw training logs.
Local SuperLink logs are a separate coordinator-side diagnostic.

## HookApps

`ds.flower.hook.run()` is available for the restricted `initial_arrays()` /
`local_update()` ABI. Arbitrary code does not receive declarative DP-SGD
granularity. If the custodian has not enabled and attested the required sandbox
and timing envelope, the client stops at the public readiness preflight before
upload. If a gate disappears after that preflight, the node refuses to open
private data and the coordinator does not accept the unchanged update as a
trained model.

## Cleanup

The high-level submission path cleans up its temporary server handles and app
uploads on both success and error. End the DataSHIELD session when finished:

```r
DSI::datashield.logout(conns)
```
